items.title: Earl Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 7, 2002
items.q: Kid Ory was even — he was out here in the early twenties.

ctx.x: Well sure. As a matter of fact I have some documentation that I can get to you. Curtis Lowe who was assistant to our Secretary/Treasurer, they commissioned him to document it, and he wrote a very, very nice documentation. It gives the local number of the first local, the first black local. And then he goes into the merger and it’s very well put. He doesn’t call names and stuff. But as I was saying before, see when I joined in 1937 the African-American black musicians, we had to join a Subsidiary Local. You got a…

saying, you had no say and also your employment was restricted. In San Francisco anything east of Divisidero the people wouldn’t hire you. See they wouldn’t hire. The club owners wouldn’t hire, and I told you that story about the Dawn Club and Wilbert Baranco. And now that’s the story that he told me. See he was directly involved. And now there was some isolated incidents, very isolated engagements where black musicians were hired. Eddie Alley, Vernon’s brother, told me a story, he worked at a place on Pacific…
